summary.en-US: Auto-delete old history, cookies, cache and site data. Pick a time limit: visits older than it, and the cookies of sites you haven't visited since, are cleared automatically. Like disappearing messages, for Firefox.

description.en-US:
Nepenthe is an automatic history cleaner and cookie cleaner for Firefox. Think disappearing messages, but for your browser: you pick a time limit (hours, days or weeks), and browsing history, cookies and site data older than that are deleted for you:

- **History:** every visit older than the limit, even on sites you still use.
- **Cookies:** every cookie of a site you haven't visited within the limit, in every container, including third-party cookies set while you were on it.
- **Site data:** local storage, IndexedDB and service workers of those sites, plus the browser cache.
- **Downloads list and recently closed tabs:** entries older than the limit. Downloaded files stay on disk.

Sites you still visit, or have open in a tab, keep their cookies so you stay signed in. A keep list protects sites you want to stay signed in to even when you rarely visit them.

**No whitelist to maintain.** Most cookie cleaners delete a site's cookies as soon as you close its tab, so you have to list every site you want to stay signed in to. Nepenthe expires cookies by when you last visited: sites you keep using stay signed in, and sites you've stopped visiting are forgotten.

**Bad night button:** forget the last few hours (12 by default) right away. Every visit, download entry, closed tab and search or form entry from that time is deleted, and sites you first visited in that time lose their cookies and site data. Sites you'd visited before keep theirs, so you stay signed in.

**Why another history cleaner?** I tried other tools and none of them worked properly, so I wrote this one. Deleting history, cookies, site storage, cache and form history is tested against a real copy of Firefox, not just assumed to work. That testing turned up the fact that Firefox's own per-site cache clearing silently does nothing, so Nepenthe clears the whole cache when a site expires rather than leaving cached files behind.

**Safe to install:** it starts switched off. Pick your limit on the settings page, and before the first run it shows exactly what will be deleted and asks you to confirm. Nepenthe keeps no record of the sites you visit and sends nothing anywhere.

**Limits:** Firefox doesn't let extensions delete search and form history once it's older than a limit (only the last few hours, which the bad night button does), so the settings page shows how to turn it off and has a button to clear what's already saved. Site permissions, bookmarks and saved passwords are left alone.

Open source (MIT): https://github.com/dirtyfilthy/nepenthe
